enzyme_name: NADPH-dependent cathinone reductase (unidentified ketoreductase of khat/Ephedra)
organism_context: Catha edulis (khat) and Ephedra spp.; only candidate aldo-keto/short-chain reductase sequences from EST and transcriptome surveys, no cloned enzyme
rationale: The (S)-cathinone -> (1S,2S)-cathine reduction is well documented metabolically in maturing khat leaves, but the reductase itself has never been purified or cloned; only the downstream N-methyltransferase of the ephedrine pathway has been characterised, so mono- vs bifunctionality cannot be judged.
direction_note: Physiological flux is cathinone -> cathine (reduction), which is the left-to-right ('>') side the council chose; KEGG R08464 writes this two-electron step with bare H+ and no NAD(P)H (ModelSEED flags CI:-2), so the eQuilibrator/GC sign that drives ModelSEED's '<' is computed on a redox-incomplete equation.

enzyme_name: NADPH-dependent cathinone reductase (unidentified ketoreductase; MetaCyc RXN-9339 of ephedrine biosynthesis)
organism_context: Ephedra sinica and Catha edulis; MetaCyc PWY-5883 lists the step without an assigned protein
rationale: Same uncharacterised ketoreductase problem as R08464: (S)-cathinone -> (1R,2S)-norephedrine is biochemically established in Ephedra and khat but no gene product has been assigned, so functionality is genuinely unknown rather than monofunctional by default.
direction_note: Biosynthesis runs cathinone -> norephedrine (the '>' side); the equation carries bare H+ instead of NADPH/NADP+ (ModelSEED CI:-2), so no thermodynamic direction computed from it is meaningful.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme (acridone prenyltransferase + O-methyltransferase + cyclase steps of acronycine formation)
organism_context: Rutaceae (Ruta graveolens, Sarcomelicope spp.) acridone alkaloid metabolism
rationale: KEGG R08471 itself is annotated 'multi-step reaction (methyltransfer, prenyltransfer and cyclizing); incomplete reaction', and ModelSEED carries it mass-unbalanced by C6H8 (the prenyl and methyl donors are absent), so there is no one protein to classify.
direction_note: The only flux that exists in vivo is biosynthetic (1,3-dihydroxy-N-methylacridone -> acronycine, the '>' side); ModelSEED's '<' would demand acronycine de-prenylation, which is not a known pathway, but the call rests on a pathway, not an enzyme.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme (acridone prenyltransferase + cyclase steps of rutacridone formation)
organism_context: Ruta graveolens acridone alkaloid metabolism
rationale: KEGG R08472 is flagged 'multi-step reaction (prenyltransfer and cyclizing); incomplete reaction' and ModelSEED carries it short by C5H6 (the dimethylallyl donor), so no single catalysing protein exists for the entry as written.
direction_note: Biosynthetic flux is 1,3-dihydroxy-N-methylacridone -> rutacridone (the '>' side); the direction is a pathway property, not an enzyme property, and the ModelSEED equation omits the prenyl donor that makes it irreversible.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme; nearest real catalyst is a type III polyketide synthase (quinolone synthase) acting on anthraniloyl-CoA + malonyl-CoA
organism_context: Rutaceae quinolone alkaloid plants; functionally equivalent fungal type III PKSs (AthePKS, FerePKS) make 2-quinolones from anthranilate derivatives in vitro
rationale: KEGG R08473 is annotated 'multi-step reaction; incomplete reaction' and ModelSEED is short by C2 and one charge because the CoA activation and the malonyl-CoA extender are both omitted; the chalcone-synthase-like PKS that does the real condensation is monofunctional but does not catalyse the written transformation.
direction_note: Anthranilate is the precursor and 4-hydroxy-2-quinolone the product in every described pathway (the '>' side); ModelSEED's '<' implies quinolone catabolism to anthranilate, for which there is no enzymology.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme (hypothetical anthranilate + 1-pyrroline route to vasicine/peganine)
organism_context: Peganum harmala / Justicia adhatoda quinazoline alkaloid biosynthesis, inferred from labelling studies only
rationale: KEGG R08477 is flagged 'multi-step reaction; incomplete reaction' and remains a precursor-feeding hypothesis with no enzyme assigned to any step; ModelSEED also carries it unbalanced (O:-1, CI:1).
direction_note: The only direction with any support is condensation of the two precursors into vasicine (the '>' side), but it is a pathway hypothesis rather than a characterised enzyme reaction.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme (alternative hypothetical N-acetylanthranilate + L-aspartate route to vasicine/peganine)
organism_context: Peganum harmala quinazoline alkaloid biosynthesis; competing labelling-based hypothesis to R08477
rationale: KEGG R08478 is annotated 'multi-step reaction; incomplete reaction', and ModelSEED's own balance check reports C:-2/H:-1/O:-6 plus a charge error, so the entry is a pathway sketch with no protein behind it.
direction_note: Flux, if any, is biosynthetic toward vasicine (the '>' side); ModelSEED's '<' comes from a group-contribution value (+292 kJ/mol) computed on a badly unbalanced equation.

enzyme_name: strictosamide-forming lactamase of camptothecin biosynthesis (unidentified; possibly partly spontaneous)
organism_context: Ophiorrhiza pumila and Camptotheca acuminata; O. pumila routes camptothecin through strictosamide, C. acuminata through strictosidinic acid
rationale: The strictosidine -> strictosamide lactamisation is an accepted step of the O. pumila camptothecin route but no catalysing protein has been isolated; KEGG marks R08487 'incomplete reaction' and the ModelSEED equation drops the methanol co-product (MI:C:-1/H:-5/O:-1).
direction_note: Lactamisation runs strictosidine -> strictosamide (the '>' side) and is driven by loss of methanol, exactly the species the ModelSEED equation omits, so its thermodynamic '<' is computed on the wrong chemistry.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme (several oxidation/ring-rearrangement steps from deoxypumiloside to camptothecin)
organism_context: Ophiorrhiza pumila / Camptotheca acuminata; the late camptothecin steps are still only candidate genes
rationale: KEGG R08490 is annotated 'multi-step reaction; incomplete reaction' and ModelSEED carries it C6H12O4 short; recent multi-omics work still only prioritises candidate genes for these late oxidations, so no single enzyme can be named.
direction_note: Biosynthesis is deoxypumiloside -> camptothecin (the '>' side); direction here is a pathway fact, and the equation is too incomplete for thermodynamics to settle it.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme (the strictosidine-to-strychnine pathway: SGD, geissoschizine synthase, Wieland-Gumlich aldehyde steps, malonyltransferase, prestrychnine decarboxylation)
organism_context: Strychnos nux-vomica; the full route was reconstituted in Nicotiana benthamiana by Hong et al. 2022
rationale: Strictosidine -> strychnine is a ten-plus enzyme pathway (deglycosylation, reduction, oxidations, malonylation, then decarboxylative cyclisation of prestrychnine), so no protein catalyses the ModelSEED entry; KEGG has since withdrawn R08495 entirely and replaced it with the stepwise reactions R13334/R13336.
direction_note: KEGG no longer serves R08495 at all, so ModelSEED is carrying a reaction its source has retired; the real pathway runs strictosidine -> strychnine (the '>' side) and is pulled irreversibly by the CO2-releasing prestrychnine step.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme (strictosidine deglycosylation plus several rearrangement/oxidation steps toward corynantheal)
organism_context: Strychnos / Corynanthe-type monoterpene indole alkaloid plants
rationale: KEGG R08496 is flagged all three ways - 'unclear reaction', 'multi-step reaction', 'incomplete reaction' - and ModelSEED carries it C8H12O8 short (the glucose moiety), so there is no single catalysing protein.
direction_note: Strictosidine is upstream of corynantheal in every described route (the '>' side); the ModelSEED equation loses the glucose released by strictosidine beta-glucosidase, which is the step that makes the sequence irreversible.

enzyme_name: unidentified (secoiridoid steps from secologanin to gentiopicroside)
organism_context: Gentiana spp. secoiridoid glycoside metabolism
rationale: KEGG explicitly labels R08500 an 'unclear reaction' and an 'incomplete reaction', and ModelSEED carries it CH4O short; no enzyme has been assigned to the secologanin -> gentiopicrin conversion.
direction_note: Secologanin is the biosynthetic precursor of gentiopicroside (the '>' side), but KEGG itself disowns the entry as unclear, so neither direction call rests on real enzymology.

enzyme_name: 3D-(3,5/4)-trihydroxycyclohexane-1,2-dione acylhydrolase (decyclizing), IolD (EC 3.7.1.22, KEGG K03336)
organism_context: Bacillus subtilis myo-inositol catabolism; orthologues in Salmonella, Sinorhizobium meliloti and many soil and commensal bacteria
rationale: IolD is a single ThDP-dependent hydrolase that performs one C-C bond cleavage, ring-opening DKDI to 5-deoxy-D-glucuronate; Yoshida et al. reconstituted the whole B. subtilis iol pathway with one discrete enzyme per step and found no second activity on IolD.
direction_note: The enzyme is a decyclising hydrolase operating in the catabolic direction (DKDI + H2O -> 5-deoxy-D-glucuronate, the '>' side); ring-opening hydrolysis is not reversed in vivo, so ModelSEED's '<' is wrong even though the equation itself is balanced.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme (polyketide synthase condensation to 5-oxo-octanal plus transamination/cyclisation to gamma-coniceine)
organism_context: Conium maculatum (poison hemlock) and Sarracenia flava; PKS candidates isolated, downstream transaminase still unassigned
rationale: KEGG R08509 is annotated 'multi-step reaction; incomplete reaction' and ModelSEED carries it unbalanced (N:+1/O:-2, CI:2) because the amine donor and malonyl-CoA extenders are missing; only part of the coniine route has been characterised, so no single protein can be classified.
direction_note: Octanoate/octanoyl units feed forward into gamma-coniceine (the '>' side); ModelSEED's '<' would be alkaloid catabolism to a fatty acid, which is not described.

enzyme_name: 4-hydroxythreonine-4-phosphate dehydrogenase, PdxA (EC 1.1.1.262)
organism_context: Escherichia coli and other gamma-proteobacteria; deoxyxylulose-dependent PLP biosynthesis (also a drug target in Acinetobacter baumannii)
rationale: PdxA is a homodimeric NAD+-dependent dehydrogenase with a single active site that oxidises 4-phosphohydroxy-L-threonine; the subsequent decarboxylation to 3-amino-2-oxopropyl phosphate is spontaneous/non-enzymatic, not a second catalytic domain, and PdxA partners PdxJ as a separate protein.
direction_note: The enzyme runs oxidatively toward 3-amino-2-oxopropyl phosphate (the '>' side) and is pulled irreversibly by CO2 loss; ModelSEED's equation omits NADH and CO2 entirely (its own check reports C:-22/H:-27/N:-7/O:-16/P:-2), which is why the ~400-600 kJ/mol 'reverse' estimate appears.

enzyme_name: pimeloyl-CoA dehydrogenase (EC 1.3.1.62; KEGG orthologues K04118 large subunit + K28556 small subunit)
organism_context: Denitrifying pimelate-degrading bacteria (Gallus & Schink isolates), Rhodopseudomonas palustris and other anaerobic benzoate degraders
rationale: This is a two-subunit acyl-CoA-dehydrogenase-family enzyme carrying one alpha,beta-desaturation activity; a two-polypeptide complex is not a fused bifunctional enzyme, so the catalytic subunit is monofunctional.
direction_note: Physiological flux is beta-oxidative, pimeloyl-CoA -> 6-carboxyhex-2-enoyl-CoA (the '>' side); ModelSEED substitutes free FAD/FADH2 for the enzyme's real NAD+/ETF-quinone acceptor, and the free-flavin couple is what produces eQuilibrator's +19 kJ/mol and hence the spurious '<'.

enzyme_name: non-decarboxylating glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase (GdhA/GcdH-type, EC 1.3.8.6 family)
organism_context: Obligately anaerobic aromatic degraders (Desulfococcus multivorans, Syntrophus, Geobacter), where glutaconyl-CoA is handed to a separate biotin-dependent glutaconyl-CoA decarboxylase
rationale: The enzyme that stops at glutaconyl-CoA is the non-decarboxylating glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase, a homotetrameric acyl-CoA dehydrogenase with a single dehydrogenation activity; Wischgoll et al. showed the decarboxylating/non-decarboxylating split is a single active-site residue, and the decarboxylating (human GCDH-like) variant would give crotonyl-CoA + CO2, not this product.
direction_note: The dehydrogenase runs glutaryl-CoA -> glutaconyl-CoA (the '>' side), electrons going to ETF and thence to the membrane quinone pool; writing free FAD/FADH2 as the acceptor is what makes eQuilibrator read +19 kJ/mol and drives ModelSEED's '<'.

enzyme_name: FAD-dependent D-lactate dehydrogenase, Dld (EC 1.1.2.4/1.1.2.5)
organism_context: Escherichia coli membrane-associated Dld, yeast mitochondrial Dld1p, Treponema pallidum TP0037 and newly mined bacterial FAD-D-LDHs
rationale: Dld-type FAD-D-LDH is a single-chain flavoprotein with one catalytic activity, oxidising D-lactate and passing electrons from its tightly bound FAD to the quinone pool or cytochrome c; its membrane association is a binding property, not a second catalytic function.
direction_note: The enzyme is a respiratory D-lactate oxidase (D-lactate -> pyruvate, the '>' side) and is effectively irreversible because the electrons leave to quinone; ModelSEED models the acceptor as free FAD/FADH2, whose low potential inverts the computed sign.

enzyme_name: salicylacetate (salicyl acetate) esterase - specific protein not identified
organism_context: none established; the generic activity (aspirin hydrolysis) is carried in mammals by carboxylesterases CES1/CES2, butyrylcholinesterase and albumin pseudo-esterase, none of which is the ModelSEED gene association
rationale: ModelSEED pairs the name 'salicylacetate esterase' with aspirin (acetylsalicylate) as substrate but saligenin (salicyl alcohol) as product, which cannot both be true - aspirin hydrolysis yields salicylate, and saligenin would require salicyl acetate as the ester; with the substrate ambiguous no catalysing protein can be identified.
direction_note: Any esterase runs hydrolytically (ester + H2O -> acid + alcohol, the '>' side) and is not reversed in water; ModelSEED's own check reports H:+2/O:-1, confirming the aspirin/salicyl-acetate mix-up that produces the large positive 'reverse' dG.

enzyme_name: 3-hydroxyadipyl-CoA dehydrogenase, PaaH (NAD+-dependent 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase of the phenylacetate catabolon)
organism_context: Escherichia coli paa operon and orthologous paa clusters in Pseudomonas and Rhodococcus; distinct from the fused bifunctional FadB of classical beta-oxidation
rationale: In the paa beta-oxidation module the hydratase (PaaF/PaaG), the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (PaaH) and the thiolase (PaaJ) are separate single-activity proteins that interact as a complex; only if this reaction is instead assigned to FadB would a genuinely fused hydratase/dehydrogenase/epimerase be involved.
direction_note: Net catabolic flux is oxidative, 3-hydroxyadipyl-CoA -> 3-oxoadipyl-CoA (the '>' side), pulled by the downstream thiolase, although NAD+-dependent 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenases are intrinsically reversible; the ModelSEED entry writes molecular H2 in place of NAD+/NADH, which is chemically meaningless and fully determines the computed sign.

enzyme_name: catalase HPII (KatE) - the protoheme-to-cis-heme d conversion is a self-catalysed modification of its own prosthetic group; no dedicated 'heme D synthase' is known
organism_context: Escherichia coli HPII (a clade-2 monofunctional catalase, unlike the genuinely bifunctional catalase-peroxidase KatG); the chemically identical heme d of cytochrome bd oxidase has no assigned biosynthetic enzyme at all
rationale: Loewen et al. showed HPII itself converts bound protoheme to cis-heme d using H2O2, i.e. an autocatalytic prosthetic-group modification inside the catalase active site rather than a separate turnover activity, so HPII stays monofunctional and there is no standalone heme D synthase to classify.
direction_note: Heme -> heme d is an irreversible oxidation (the '>' side) requiring H2O2/O2, but the ModelSEED equation writes it as a bare hydration with no oxidant, so the +115 kJ/mol dGPredictor value behind ModelSEED's '<' describes a reaction that does not exist.

enzyme_name: FAD-linked mitochondrial glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (Gut2p in yeast; GPD2/mGPDH in mammals, EC 1.1.5.3)
organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Gut2p on the outer face of the inner mitochondrial membrane; mammalian mGPDH, the metformin target
rationale: A single flavoprotein chain with one catalytic activity, oxidising glycerol-3-phosphate and reducing ubiquinone; the mammalian enzyme's EF-hand Ca2+-binding region is regulatory, not a second catalytic site, so it does not count as bifunctional.
direction_note: mGPDH/Gut2p is the oxidative arm of the glycerophosphate shuttle (G3P -> DHAP, the '>' side) and is irreversible because electrons leave to CoQ; the cytosolic NAD-linked Gpd1p runs the opposite way as a separate enzyme, and modelling the acceptor as free FAD/FADH2 is what makes eQuilibrator return +11 kJ/mol and ModelSEED choose '<'.

enzyme_name: dihydroxy-acid dehydratase (Ilv3p/IlvD, EC 4.2.1.9)
organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae mitochondrial Ilv3p; bacterial and plant IlvD orthologues (a herbicide/antimicrobial target)
rationale: DHAD is a single [Fe-S]-cluster dehydratase with one catalytic activity (dehydration of 2,3-dihydroxy-3-methylbutanoate to 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate); no second activity is reported in the structural or inhibitor literature.
direction_note: DHAD is the committed, effectively irreversible dehydration step toward 2-oxoisovalerate (the '>' side); the ModelSEED entry names the ketol-acid reductoisomerase intermediate 3-hydroxy-3-methyl-2-oxobutanoate as substrate and omits both NADPH and water (its own check reports O:-1), so it is not actually the DHAD reaction.

enzyme_name: glucan 1,4-alpha-glucosidase (glucoamylase), vacuolar Sga1p (EC 3.2.1.3)
organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae sporulation-specific vacuolar glucoamylase; GH15 family, as in Aspergillus GlaA
rationale: A single exo-acting glycoside hydrolase activity releasing glucose from the non-reducing end; the starch-binding module carried by many fungal glucoamylases is a non-catalytic CBM, so it does not make the enzyme bifunctional.
direction_note: Glycosidic hydrolysis runs one way in vivo (glycogen + H2O -> glucose, the '>' side); ModelSEED's '<' is an artefact of the glycogen pseudo-compound (C24H42O21) being consumed whole without a shortened-polymer product (its own check reports C:-18/H:-32/O:-16), which is exactly what inflates the dG to +220 to +532 kJ/mol.

enzyme_name: glycogen phosphorylase (EC 2.4.1.1; bacterial maltodextrin phosphorylase MalP, yeast Gph1p, animal PYGL/PYGM/PYGB)
organism_context: Broadly conserved; the PLP cofactor acts as a general acid/base rather than in transamination
rationale: One catalytic activity, phosphorolysis of the alpha-1,4 glycosidic bond; the allosteric AMP/glucose-6-phosphate sites and the Ser14 phosphorylation site are regulatory, and the debranching enzyme's genuinely bifunctional transferase/glucosidase is a different protein.
direction_note: Phosphorylase sits near equilibrium (dG'o around +3 kJ/mol) and its in vivo direction is set by the Pi:glucose-1-phosphate ratio, not by the enzyme - though the physiological net flux is phosphorolytic, so of the two options the council's '>' is the better one; ModelSEED's '<' is driven by the same unbalanced glycogen pseudo-compound (C:-18/H:-32/O:-16) that gives the nonsensical +225 to +525 kJ/mol.
